source.original_text:
Let A(x)=-x on E=R^I, where I is finite. For every real-valued ambient function f and every w,h∈E, the first derivative of f∘A at w applied to h equals -Df(-w)[h]. The existing extrinsic spherical differential expression commutes with reflection: L_S(f∘A)(w)=L_Sf(-w). These equalities use the total Mathlib derivative operators. In the classical smooth setting at unit points, they give the familiar reflection symmetry of the spherical generator.

I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality, and E is the real Euclidean space with coordinates indexed by I.
f:E→R and w∈E are arbitrary; the first identity quantifies every direction h∈E. No smoothness, unit-norm or positive-dimension premise is imposed on the total-operator identity.
The radial correction uses max(|I|−1,0), implemented by natural-number subtraction before conversion to R.

D(f\circ A)(w)[h]=-Df(-w)[h],\qquad \mathcal L_S(f\circ A)(w)=\mathcal L_Sf(-w).

This is a transport identity for total ambient differential expressions. It does not assert that an arbitrary f has classical derivatives, nor construct an intrinsic Laplace–Beltrami operator, diffusion, invariant measure, evolution-equation solution or log-Sobolev inequality. Classical sphere applications separately supply C2 tests and unit points.

lean.statement:
anonymous_statement : ∀
  {I : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ I),
  (∀ (h : EuclideanSpace ℝ I), (fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) w) h = -(fderiv ℝ f (-w)) h) ∧
    object_1 (fun x => f (-x)) w =
      object_1 f (-w)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let I be any finite type with decidable equality, possibly empty, and let E=R^I be its finite-dimensional real Euclidean coordinate space. Let n=|I| be its cardinality as a natural number, and let b be the real cast of n dotminus 1, where dotminus denotes truncated subtraction in N. Let f:E->R be any function and w any point of E. No continuity, differentiability, measurability, unit-norm or nonzero-dimensionality condition is assumed.

Write Df(x)=fderiv_R f(x), a continuous real linear map from E to R, using Mathlib's total Frechet derivative. Thus Df(x) is the derivative when f is differentiable at x and is the zero continuous linear map otherwise. Write D2f(x)[a,beta]=(fderiv_R (x->Df(x))(x)[a])[beta]. This is the total derivative of the derivative-valued function, first applied to a and then to beta. Its totalization is applied to the function x->Df(x) itself; no classical twice-differentiability assertion is implicit. Let Delta f(x) be the actual Laplacian contraction of this total second derivative, equivalently sum_{i in I}D2f(x)[e_i,e_i] in the standard orthonormal coordinate basis.

Define the real-valued operator T by
T(f)(x)=Delta f(x)-D2f(x)[x,x]-b*Df(x)[x].
This is the exact literal definition of the anonymous object. In particular, the coefficient is the cast of the natural number n dotminus 1, not an unconditional real subtraction n_R-1.

Set g(x)=f(-x), with literal vector negation. Then both conclusions hold: for every h in E,
Dg(w)[h]=-Df(-w)[h],
and
T(g)(w)=T(f)(-w).
Equivalently, the first identity says that the total continuous linear maps satisfy Dg(w)=-Df(-w). In fully expanded form the second identity is
Delta g(w)-D2g(w)[w,w]-b*Dg(w)[w] = Delta f(-w)-D2f(-w)[-w,-w]-b*Df(-w)[-w].
Both are exact pointwise identities for all the stated functions and points, without exceptional sets or measure-theoretic quantifiers.

The operator identity compares the reflected function at w with the original function at -w. It does not assert T(f)(w)=T(f)(-w) for an arbitrary unreflected function, and no evenness assumption on f is present. The operator is defined on the whole ambient Euclidean space, and the conclusion is not restricted to the unit sphere. The theorem supplies neither classical differentiability nor regularity of f or g; its unconditional meaning depends on the explicitly totalized derivatives and Laplacian. No separately defined intrinsic geometric operator or coordinate-free extension is required to interpret the statement.

The only dimension-dependent coefficient is b=max(n-1,0), cast to R. If I is empty, n=0 and b=0 rather than -1; E has just its zero vector, the basis sum is empty, all the displayed derivatives and T are zero, and both identities remain valid. If n=1, b is also zero, so only the Laplacian and the radial second-derivative term remain in T. There is no lower bound on n and no quantitative estimate, unspecified constant, normalization or asymptotic parameter in the conclusion.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereDiffusionGenerator
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Equiv

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereAntipodalGenerator

open SphereDiffusionGenerator
open scoped Laplacian

/-- Negation transports the actual first derivative and commutes with the
existing extrinsic sphere expression. These are total-operator identities;
classical generator applications separately supply smooth tests and unit points. -/
theorem sphere_differential_operators_comp_neg
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
    (∀ h : EuclideanSpace ℝ I,
      fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) w h = -fderiv ℝ f (-w) h) ∧
    sphereLaplacian (fun x => f (-x)) w = sphereLaplacian f (-w) := by
  have hD (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y)) x = -fderiv ℝ f (-x) := by
    simpa only [neg_one_smul] using (fderiv_comp_smul (f := f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ))
  have hDfun : fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) = fun x => -fderiv ℝ f (-x) :=
    funext hD
  have hH (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y))) x = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (-x) := by
    rw [hDfun]
    change fderiv ℝ (-(fun y => fderiv ℝ f (-y))) x = _
    rw [fderiv_neg]
    have ht := fderiv_comp_smul (f := fderiv ℝ f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ)
    simpa only [neg_one_smul, neg_neg] using congrArg (fun L => -L) ht
  have hLap : (Δ (fun x => f (-x))) w = (Δ f) (-w) := by
    rw [InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ),
      InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ)]
    simp only [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one, hH]
  constructor
  · intro h
    simpa only [neg_apply] using congrArg (fun L => L h) (hD w)
  · simp only [sphereLaplacian, hLap, hH, hD, neg_apply,
      map_neg, neg_neg]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereAntipodalGenerator

steps.title: Transport the first derivative
steps.text: Negation is multiplication by the nonzero scalar -1. Mathlib transports the total derivative through this invertible change of variables, including the nondifferentiable cases handled by its total definition.
steps.lean:
have hD (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y)) x = -fderiv ℝ f (-x) := by
    simpa only [neg_one_smul] using (fderiv_comp_smul (f := f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ))

steps.title: Differentiate the transported derivative
steps.text: The first derivative is the function x↦-Df(-x). Applying total derivative transport once more introduces a second minus sign; the two signs cancel. This gives equality of the actual continuous bilinear derivative expressions.
steps.lean:
have hDfun : fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) = fun x => -fderiv ℝ f (-x) :=
    funext hD
  have hH (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :

    simpa only [neg_one_smul, neg_neg] using congrArg (fun L => -L) ht

steps.title: Contract and remove the radial terms
steps.text: The ambient Laplacian is the finite diagonal sum of the second derivative in an orthonormal basis, so its reflected value agrees. Bilinearity cancels the two signs in the radial Hessian. The sign of the first derivative is absorbed by replacing the radial vector w by -w. Substitute these three identities into the existing sphere expression.
